--- title: "Feature Engineering, Explainability & HPO" description: "Automated feature engineering (target transform, permutation importance, interaction discovery, pruning), SHAP explainability, leakage detection, and hyperparameter optimization." date: today format: html: self-contained: true embed-resources: true code-fold: true code-tools: true --- This notebook covers the **analysis and optimization** layer of iter8ml: 1. **Target Transformation** — detect and fix skewed targets 2. **Automated Feature Engineering** — top-K selection, interaction discovery, pruning 3. **Leakage Detection** — flag features that may leak target information 4. **SHAP Explainability** — global feature importance with beeswarm and dependence plots 5. **Hyperparameter Optimization** — Optuna-based HPO with parameter importance ## 1. Prepare Data ::: {#prepare-data .cell cache='true' execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import polars as pl from sklearn.datasets import make_classification from iter8ml.data.adapter import DataAdapter X_raw, y_raw = make_classification( n_samples=3000, n_features=20, n_informative=12, random_state=42 ) feature_names = [f"feat_{i}" for i in range(X_raw.shape[1])] df = pl.DataFrame({f"feat_{i}": X_raw[:, i] for i in range(X_raw.shape[1])}) df = df.with_columns(target=pl.Series(y_raw)) adapter = DataAdapter() X, y = adapter.transform(df, "target") print(f"X: {X.shape}, y: {y.shape}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` X: (3000, 20), y: (3000,) ``` ::: ::: ## 2. Target Transformation ::: {#cell-target-transform .cell fig-height='4' fig-width='10' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from iter8ml.data.features import detect_target_skewness, transform_target np.random.seed(42) y_skewed = np.exp(np.random.randn(3000)) skew_before = detect_target_skewness(y_skewed) y_transformed, transform_result, _ = transform_target(y_skewed, method="auto") fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4)) axes[0].hist(y_skewed, bins=50, color="#4C72B0", alpha=0.8) axes[0].set_title(f"Original Target (skew={skew_before:.2f})") axes[0].set_ylabel("Count") axes[1].hist(y_transformed, bins=50, color="#55A868", alpha=0.8) axes[1].set_title(f"Transformed ({transform_result.method}, skew={transform_result.transformed_skewness:.2f})") axes[1].set_ylabel("Count") plt.suptitle("Target Transformation: Fixing Skewed Distributions", fontsize=12, y=1.02) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() print(f"Method: {transform_result.method} | Applied: {transform_result.applied} | " f"Skewness: {transform_result.original_skewness:.2f} -> {transform_result.transformed_skewness:.2f}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Target distribution before and after transformation (skewed regression target)](05_feature_engineering_explainability_files/figure-html/target-transform-output-1.png){#target-transform width=950 height=396} ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Method: box-cox | Applied: True | Skewness: 7.73 -> -0.00 ``` ::: ::: ## 3. Top-K Feature Selection ::: {#top-k-selection .cell cache='true' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from iter8ml.engine.models.factory import get_model_class from iter8ml.data.features import extract_top_k_features model_cls = get_model_class("lightgbm") model = model_cls(task="classification") model.fit(X, y) top_k_indices = extract_top_k_features( model, X, y, k=10, feature_names=feature_names, task="classification" ) print(f"Top-10 feature indices: {top_k_indices}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Top-10 feature indices: [0, 14, 9, 8, 2, 11, 19, 5, 16, 4] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-permutation-importance-chart .cell fig-height='5' fig-width='8' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance if hasattr(model, "_estimator_type"): sk_model = model elif hasattr(model, "_model") and hasattr(model._model, "fit"): sk_model = model._model else: from iter8ml.data.features import _to_sklearn_estimator sk_model = _to_sklearn_estimator(model, "classification") perm_result = permutation_importance(sk_model, X, y, n_repeats=10, random_state=42, scoring="roc_auc") sorted_idx = perm_result.importances_mean.argsort()[::-1][:10] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5)) top_names = [feature_names[i] for i in sorted_idx] top_importances = perm_result.importances_mean[sorted_idx] ax.barh(top_names, top_importances, color="#4C72B0") ax.set_xlabel("Mean Permutation Importance") ax.set_title("Top-10 Features by Permutation Importance") ax.invert_yaxis() ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.3) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Top-10 features by permutation importance — measures how much model performance drops when each feature is shuffled](05_feature_engineering_explainability_files/figure-html/permutation-importance-chart-output-1.png){#permutation-importance-chart width=756 height=470} ::: ::: ## 4. Feature Pruning ::: {#feature-pruning .cell cache='true' execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} from iter8ml.data.features import prune_features X_full = np.hstack([X, X_aug]) full_feature_names = feature_names + interaction_result.new_feature_names prune_model = model_cls(task="classification") prune_model.fit(X_full, y) X_pruned, pruning_result = prune_features( prune_model, X_full, y, feature_names=full_feature_names, task="classification" ) print(f"Original features: {pruning_result.n_original} | " f"Kept: {pruning_result.n_kept} | Dropped: {pruning_result.n_dropped}") if pruning_result.dropped_features: print(f"Dropped: {pruning_result.dropped_features}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Original features: 24 | Kept: 1 | Dropped: 23 Dropped: ['feat_0', 'feat_1', 'feat_2', 'feat_3', 'feat_4', 'feat_5', 'feat_6', 'feat_7', 'feat_8', 'feat_9', 'feat_10', 'feat_11', 'feat_12', 'feat_13', 'feat_15', 'feat_16', 'feat_17', 'feat_18', 'feat_19', 'feat_0_multiply_feat_9', 'feat_0_multiply_feat_2', 'feat_9_multiply_feat_2', 'feat_8_multiply_feat_2'] ``` ::: ::: ## 6. Leakage Detection ::: {#leakage-detection .cell cache='true' execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} from iter8ml.data.leakage import detect_leakage leakage_report = detect_leakage(X, y, task="classification", threshold=0.15) print(f"Baseline score: {leakage_report.baseline_score:.4f} | " f"Features flagged: {leakage_report.n_flagged}/{leakage_report.n_features_tested}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Baseline score: 0.8931 | Features flagged: 0/20 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-leakage-chart .cell fig-height='5' fig-width='8' execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score rng = np.random.RandomState(42) baseline_scores_cv = cross_val_score( LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42), X, y, cv=3, scoring="roc_auc" ) baseline_mean = float(np.mean(baseline_scores_cv)) drops = [] X_work = X.copy() for col in range(X.shape[1]): orig = X_work[:, col].copy() rng.shuffle(X_work[:, col]) perm_scores = cross_val_score( LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42), X_work, y, cv=3, scoring="roc_auc" ) X_work[:, col] = orig drops.append(baseline_mean - float(np.mean(perm_scores))) sorted_pairs = sorted(enumerate(drops), key=lambda p: p[1], reverse=True) sorted_idx, sorted_drops = zip(*sorted_pairs) flag_colors = ["#C44E52" if d > 0.15 else "#4C72B0" for d in sorted_drops] fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5)) ax.barh([feature_names[i] for i in sorted_idx], sorted_drops, color=flag_colors) ax.axvline(0.15, color="#C44E52", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5, label="Leakage threshold (0.15)") ax.set_xlabel("Score Drop (ROC AUC)") ax.set_title("Leakage Detection — Permutation Score Drop per Feature") ax.legend(fontsize=8) ax.invert_yaxis() ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.3) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Per-feature score drop when each feature is permuted — large drops may indicate data leakage](05_feature_engineering_explainability_files/figure-html/leakage-chart-output-1.png){#leakage-chart width=758 height=470} ::: ::: ## 7. SHAP Explainability ::: {#shap-setup .cell cache='true' execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} from iter8ml.analysis.explainability import Explainer explainer = Explainer(model, feature_names=feature_names) shap_result = explainer.explain(X[:500], run_id="notebook_nb04", max_display=15, generate_plots=False) print(f"Model: {shap_result.model_name} | Features: {shap_result.n_features}") print("\nTop-10 features by SHAP importance:") for f in shap_result.top_features[:10]: print(f" {f.feature_name:12s} importance={f.importance:.6f}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Model: LightGBM | Features: 20 Top-10 features by SHAP importance: feat_5 importance=3.059614 feat_14 importance=2.943352 feat_0 importance=2.034318 feat_11 importance=2.007593 feat_8 importance=1.789522 feat_16 importance=1.696965 feat_19 importance=1.665619 feat_2 importance=1.571072 feat_6 importance=1.551637 feat_17 importance=1.519457 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-shap-beeswarm .cell fig-height='6' fig-width='10' execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} import shap shap_explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model._model) shap_values = shap_explainer(X[:500]) plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6)) shap.plots.beeswarm(shap_values, max_display=15, show=False) plt.title("SHAP Feature Importance (Beeswarm)") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![SHAP beeswarm plot — each dot is a sample; color shows feature value (red=high, blue=low); x-axis shows SHAP value (impact on prediction)](05_feature_engineering_explainability_files/figure-html/shap-beeswarm-output-1.png){#shap-beeswarm width=743 height=708} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-shap-dependence .cell fig-height='3.5' fig-width='12' execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} top3_names = [f.feature_name for f in shap_result.top_features[:3]] top3_indices = [feature_names.index(n) for n in top3_names] fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.5)) for ax, feat_idx, feat_name in zip(axes, top3_indices, top3_names): feat_vals = X[:500, feat_idx] shap_vals = shap_values.values[:, feat_idx] sc = ax.scatter(feat_vals, shap_vals, c=feat_vals, cmap="coolwarm", alpha=0.4, s=8) ax.set_xlabel(feat_name) ax.set_ylabel("SHAP value") ax.set_title(feat_name, fontsize=10) ax.axhline(0, color="gray", linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.5) ax.grid(alpha=0.2) plt.suptitle("SHAP Dependence Plots", fontsize=12, y=1.02) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![SHAP dependence plots for top-3 features — shows how feature value relates to model impact](05_feature_engineering_explainability_files/figure-html/shap-dependence-output-1.png){#shap-dependence width=1155 height=348} ::: ::: ## 8. Hyperparameter Optimization ::: {#hpo-setup .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} from iter8ml.engine.hpo import create_study, optimize_model from iter8ml.engine.evaluator import Evaluator from iter8ml.config import ExperimentConfig hpo_config = ExperimentConfig( name="hpo_nb", task="classification", target_col="target", data_path="", cv_folds=3, metrics=["roc_auc"], ) evaluator = Evaluator(hpo_config) print("HPO configured — 3-fold CV with ROC AUC") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` HPO configured — 3-fold CV with ROC AUC ``` ::: ::: ::: {#hpo-run .cell cache='true' execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} from iter8ml.engine.models.factory import get_model_class as GMC model_cls = GMC("catboost") hpo_result = optimize_model( model_cls, X, y, evaluator, "catboost", n_trials=15, task="classification", ) print(f"Best ROC AUC: {hpo_result['best_value']:.4f}") print("Best parameters:") for k, v in hpo_result["best_params"].items(): print(f" {k}: {v}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}
